newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - April 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post business - April 16.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following items on the front page of its business section on April 16:
NEW YORK - The stock market surged, propelled by glowing corporate earnings and a better-than-expected report on consumer prices that convinced some investors that inflation is not a problem.
WASHINGTON - As federal agencies debate the safety of air bags, the Clinton administration is launching a campaign to increase seat-belt use.
NEW YORK - Dow Jones & Co. is expected to usher in an era of tougher scrutiny of management decisions when shareholders elect four new members to the company's board.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. - Intel Corp. said it has passed an important new milestone in the quest to make computer chips smaller and faster, developing technology to manufacture chips with transistors that are 1/400th as wide as a human hair.

DALLAS - An informal survey conducted by the American Management Association for its conference in Dallas shows that nearly half of its 400 participants -- a broad cross-section of middle-sized and large American companies and 50 government agencies -- said skilled manpower is in short supply.
